items.q: The laboratory's verdict was ______: the bone fragments were at least forty thousand years old.
items.vi: Kết luận của phòng thí nghiệm là không thể chối cãi: các mảnh xương có niên đại ít nhất bốn mươi nghìn năm.
items.explanation: Word choice: the colon introduces a definite finding (at least forty thousand years old), so the verdict left no doubt — unequivocal = clear, leaving no room for doubt. ✗ equivocal — ambiguous, open to two readings, the opposite of the clue; ✗ equivalent — equal in value or amount, nothing to do with certainty; ✗ ambivalent — having mixed feelings, said of a person, not of a verdict.

items.q: For almost a decade the data broker operated ______, compiling profiles that most users never knew existed.
items.vi: Trong gần một thập kỷ, công ty môi giới dữ liệu ấy hoạt động âm thầm ngoài tầm chú ý, lập những hồ sơ mà hầu hết người dùng chưa từng biết là có.
items.explanation: Idiom: the clue is profiles that most users never knew existed, so the broker escaped notice — under the radar = unnoticed, without attracting attention. ✗ off the hook — freed from blame or a duty; ✗ on the fence — undecided between two sides; ✗ up in the air — not yet settled or decided. None describes working unnoticed for years.

items.q: The builders of the tomb ______ have used wheeled carts, since no trace of a wheel has ever been found in the region.
items.vi: Những người xây lăng mộ này không thể nào đã dùng xe có bánh, vì chưa từng tìm thấy dấu vết bánh xe nào trong vùng.
items.explanation: Modal deduction about the past: no trace of a wheel has ever been found is evidence, so the speaker concludes it was impossible — can't have + past participle = "I am sure this did not happen". ✗ mustn't have — must have deduces that something DID happen; its negative is can't have; ✗ needn't have — it was unnecessary but they did it; ✗ shouldn't have — it was a mistake to do it; neither says what was possible.

items.q: Broadcasting your location in real time ______ a serious risk to your personal safety.
items.vi: Việc phát vị trí của bạn theo thời gian thực gây ra một rủi ro nghiêm trọng cho an toàn cá nhân.
items.explanation: Collocation with risk: a danger poses a risk/threat to someone — pose = present, cause. ✗ puts — the pattern is put someone at risk, and here the object is a risk, not a person; ✗ makes — make a risk is not English (we take or run a risk); ✗ does — do a risk does not exist.

items.q: With no witnesses and no fingerprints, the case against the hacker rested entirely on ______ evidence.
items.vi: Không có nhân chứng và không có dấu vân tay, vụ án chống lại tin tặc ấy hoàn toàn dựa vào bằng chứng gián tiếp.
items.explanation: Word choice: no witnesses and no fingerprints means the evidence is indirect — circumstantial evidence = facts that suggest guilt without proving it directly. ✗ coincidental — happening by chance at the same time; ✗ incidental — minor, secondary, by the way; ✗ accidental — unintended, by accident; none is a term used with evidence in court.

items.q: The deal to digitise the museum's entire archive ______ when the main sponsor withdrew at the last minute.
items.vi: Thỏa thuận số hóa toàn bộ kho lưu trữ của bảo tàng đã đổ bể khi nhà tài trợ chính rút lui vào phút chót.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb with fall: the clue the main sponsor withdrew tells you the deal failed — fell through = (of a plan or deal) failed to happen. ✗ fell out — quarrelled with someone; ✗ fell behind — failed to keep up, got behind schedule; ✗ fell off — declined in number or quality.

items.q: ______ had the probe been launched than contact with it was lost.
items.vi: Tàu thăm dò vừa mới được phóng lên thì đã mất liên lạc.
items.explanation: Inversion: the clue is than later in the sentence, so the pattern is No sooner had … than … = "as soon as". ✗ Hardly — Hardly had … when … needs when, not than; ✗ Not until — inverts the MAIN clause (Not until X was contact lost), not the clause it introduces; ✗ Only when — same problem, and it never pairs with than.

items.q: Rather than cut down gradually, he decided to ______ and deleted every social media app from his phone in a single evening.
items.vi: Thay vì giảm dần, anh ấy quyết định cai hẳn một lần và xóa toàn bộ ứng dụng mạng xã hội khỏi điện thoại chỉ trong một buổi tối.
items.explanation: Idiom with go: Rather than cut down gradually and in a single evening show he stopped all at once — go cold turkey = quit a habit suddenly and completely. ✗ go the extra mile — make more effort than required; ✗ go with the flow — accept things as they come; ✗ go through the roof — (of prices) rise sharply, or (of a person) explode with anger.

items.q: The privacy cost of a single photo upload may seem ______, but every post adds another data point to your profile.
items.vi: Cái giá về quyền riêng tư của một lần tải ảnh lên có vẻ không đáng kể, nhưng mỗi bài đăng lại thêm một điểm dữ liệu vào hồ sơ của bạn.
items.explanation: Word family of neglect: the contrast may seem … but every post adds means the cost looks tiny — negligible = too small to matter. ✗ negligent — (of a person) careless, failing in a duty; ✗ neglected — not looked after (a neglected garden); ✗ neglectful — habitually careless about someone or something. Only negligible describes size.

items.q: Each new leak ______ the stakes, ______ regulators to act sooner than they had planned.
items.vi: Mỗi vụ rò rỉ mới lại nâng cao mức độ rủi ro, buộc các cơ quan quản lý phải hành động sớm hơn dự kiến.
items.explanation: Double blank: the stakes is an object, so the verb must be transitive raised (rise takes no object); the second blank has no conjunction before it, so the participle forcing shows the result. ✗ rose / forced — rose cannot take an object; ✗ raised / forced — two finite verbs (raised … forced) would need and between them; ✗ rose / forcing — rose is intransitive.

items.q: The regulator demanded that the company ______ fully transparent about which third parties receive users' data.
items.vi: Cơ quan quản lý yêu cầu công ty phải hoàn toàn minh bạch về việc những bên thứ ba nào nhận được dữ liệu của người dùng.
items.explanation: Subjunctive: after demanded that (a verb of demand or suggestion) the verb is the base form be, whatever the subject or tense. ✗ is — present indicative, not used after demand that; ✗ was — past indicative, same problem; ✗ were — this is the if I were subjunctive for unreal conditions, not the form used after demand.

items.q: The pottery unearthed at the site ______ a striking resemblance to designs found five hundred kilometres away.
items.vi: Đồ gốm khai quật tại di chỉ này mang nét tương đồng đáng kinh ngạc với các hoa văn được tìm thấy cách đó năm trăm cây số.
items.explanation: Collocation: a striking resemblance to takes the fixed verb bear — bear a resemblance to = look like. ✗ holds — you hold a view or a record, not a resemblance; ✗ carries — you carry weight or a risk; ✗ keeps — you keep a promise or a secret. None of these verbs collocates with resemblance.

items.q: The team had located the tomb in 2015 but, rather than dig at once, chose to ______ until better scanning technology became available.
items.vi: Nhóm nghiên cứu đã xác định được vị trí lăng mộ từ năm 2015 nhưng, thay vì đào ngay, họ chọn kiên nhẫn chờ thời cơ cho đến khi có công nghệ quét tốt hơn.
items.explanation: Idiom: rather than dig at once and until better scanning technology became available show patient waiting — bide your time = wait calmly for the right moment. ✗ cut your losses — give up before losing even more; ✗ pull your weight — do your fair share of the work; ✗ mend your fences — repair a damaged relationship.

items.q: The historian's claim that the city had a written language remained ______ until the clay tablets were finally deciphered.
items.vi: Luận điểm của nhà sử học rằng thành phố này từng có chữ viết vẫn chưa được chứng thực cho đến khi các phiến đất sét cuối cùng được giải mã.
items.explanation: Word family of substance: until the clay tablets were finally deciphered tells you the claim lacked proof — unsubstantiated = not supported by evidence. ✗ insubstantial — flimsy, lacking solidity or importance; ✗ substantive — real, dealing with essentials; ✗ substantial — large in size or amount. Only unsubstantiated describes a claim without proof.

items.q: The site's founders now openly regret ______ user data to advertisers in the company's early years.
items.vi: Những người sáng lập trang web giờ đây công khai hối tiếc vì đã bán dữ liệu người dùng cho các nhà quảng cáo trong những năm đầu của công ty.
items.explanation: Gerund vs infinitive after regret: the selling happened in the company's early years, so they regret a past action — regret + -ing = feel sorry about something already done. ✗ to sell — regret to + infinitive announces bad news now (we regret to inform you); ✗ sell — regret never takes a bare infinitive; ✗ to have sold — the perfect infinitive is not used after regret; for a past action say selling or having sold.

items.q: Every day the site's servers must ______ thousands of automated login attempts from hijacked computers.
items.vi: Mỗi ngày, máy chủ của trang web phải chống đỡ hàng nghìn lượt đăng nhập tự động từ các máy tính bị chiếm quyền điều khiển.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: the servers face automated login attempts (an attack) and must repel them — fend off = drive away, keep off. ✗ fend for — only in fend for yourself = look after yourself; ✗ put off — postpone, or discourage someone; ✗ set off — trigger (an alarm) or start a journey.

items.q: ______ with the paper surveys of the 1990s, today's online census forms take barely ten minutes to complete.
items.vi: So với các phiếu khảo sát giấy của thập niên 1990, mẫu điều tra dân số trực tuyến ngày nay chỉ mất chưa đầy mười phút để hoàn thành.
items.explanation: Participle clause: the subject today's online census forms is the thing being compared, so the past (passive) participle Compared with is needed. ✗ Comparing — an active participle would make the forms the ones doing the comparing; ✗ To compare — an infinitive of purpose ("in order to compare") makes no sense here; ✗ Having compared — also active, so the forms would again be the comparers.

items.q: Once the researchers had ______ how the algorithm ranked posts, they ______ that outrage was being rewarded.
items.vi: Một khi các nhà nghiên cứu đã hiểu ra cách thuật toán xếp hạng bài đăng, họ nhận ra rằng sự phẫn nộ đang được tưởng thưởng.
items.explanation: Double blank: how the algorithm ranked posts is something you understand or solve, so figured out; the main clause after Once … needs a finite past verb, realised. ✗ figured in / realised — figure in = include, play a part; ✗ figured on / to realise — figure on = expect, and an infinitive cannot be the main verb; ✗ worked out / realising — worked out fits, but the participle leaves no main verb.

items.q: ______ carefully a password is chosen, it is worthless once it has been reused on a dozen sites.
items.vi: Dù mật khẩu được chọn cẩn thận đến đâu, nó cũng trở nên vô giá trị một khi đã được dùng lại trên cả chục trang web.
items.explanation: Concession of degree: the blank is followed directly by an adverb, carefully, so use No matter how + adverb (= however carefully). ✗ However much — much cannot sit in front of another adverb (however carefully works; however much carefully does not); ✗ Whatever — needs a noun (whatever password), not an adverb; ✗ Even though — a conjunction that needs a full clause, not carefully straight after it.

items.q: By selling the family farm to fund the expedition, the explorer had ______: there was simply no going back.
options: burnt a hole in his pocket
items.vi: Bằng việc bán nông trại của gia đình để tài trợ cho chuyến thám hiểm, nhà thám hiểm đã tự đốt thuyền chặt đứt đường lui: đơn giản là không còn đường quay về nữa.
items.explanation: Idiom with burn: the colon explains it — there was simply no going back — so burn your boats (= burn your bridges) = act so that retreat is impossible. ✗ burn your fingers — get hurt by a risky venture; ✗ burn the midnight oil — work or study late into the night; ✗ burn a hole in your pocket — (of money) tempt you to spend it at once.

items.q: Radiocarbon dating gave the team ______ grounds for redating the temple by three centuries.
items.vi: Phương pháp định tuổi bằng carbon phóng xạ đã cho nhóm nghiên cứu những cơ sở rất thuyết phục để xác định lại niên đại ngôi đền, chênh lệch tới ba thế kỷ.
items.explanation: Word family of compel: grounds for redating must be convincing — compelling = very convincing (compelling evidence, reasons). ✗ compulsive — driven by an uncontrollable urge (a compulsive liar); ✗ compulsory — required by rule (compulsory education); ✗ compelled — forced to do something, said of a person, not of grounds.

items.q: Neither the archaeologists nor the museum director ______ willing to say when the sealed chamber will be opened.
items.vi: Cả các nhà khảo cổ lẫn giám đốc bảo tàng đều không sẵn lòng cho biết khi nào căn phòng bị niêm phong sẽ được mở.
items.explanation: Agreement with neither … nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the singular museum director, and the sentence is about now (will be opened), so is. ✗ are — plural, but the nearer subject is singular; ✗ were — plural and past, while the situation is present; ✗ have been — plural present perfect, agreeing with archaeologists, the farther subject.

items.q: The more personal data a platform collects, ______ it becomes to advertisers.
items.vi: Nền tảng càng thu thập nhiều dữ liệu cá nhân thì càng trở nên có giá trị đối với các nhà quảng cáo.
items.explanation: Double comparative: The more … a platform collects must be balanced by the more valuable — both halves need the + comparative. ✗ the most valuable — a superlative, not a comparative; ✗ more valuable — the second half also needs the; ✗ the more valuably — becomes is a linking verb and takes an adjective, not an adverb.

items.q: After months of checks, the physicists ______ the conclusion that the signal was nothing more than noise from a nearby fridge.
items.vi: Sau nhiều tháng kiểm tra, các nhà vật lý đi đến kết luận rằng tín hiệu đó chẳng qua chỉ là nhiễu từ một chiếc tủ lạnh gần đó.
items.explanation: Collocation with conclusion: there is no preposition before the conclusion, and only reach takes the noun directly — reach the conclusion that. ✗ arrived — needs at (arrived at the conclusion); ✗ came — needs to (came to the conclusion); ✗ got — needs to as well, and is informal.

items.q: By the end of the decade, most routine scans ______ by algorithms rather than by radiologists.
items.vi: Đến cuối thập kỷ này, hầu hết các ảnh chụp thường quy sẽ được thuật toán đọc thay vì bác sĩ chẩn đoán hình ảnh.
items.explanation: Future perfect passive: By the end of the decade sets a future deadline, and by algorithms shows the scans receive the action — will have been read. ✗ will have read — active, making the scans the readers; ✗ will be reading — active and continuous, same problem, and no completion by the deadline; ✗ have been read — passive but present perfect, ignoring the future time marker.
